title: LiveMath meta-option (D1) policy: a tested boundary between task-structure and answer-distribution rules; the structural rule gains on meta items but cannot be told apart from the forbidden blind rule on this pool
verdict_cn: 结论：能做，但收益小（可行性中等）。LiveMath是数学选择题，常有一个固定选项“其余选项中有一个是对的，但还能证明更强的结论”。全部283道训练题中它出现129次，129次都是正确答案，这是题库本身的规律。上一轮LiveMath失败的63%是“该选它却没选”：模型约一半根本没提它，三分之一当凑数项打发，六成自称“记得原定理”而挑了被削弱的说法；“结果对不上任何选项”的只有164次中的4次，且都选了“最接近的”。允许的规则须同时满足三条：只依据题目说明和选项字面意思；只有模型在本题指出具体削弱处（多了条件、范围变窄、界变差等）才推荐它；无论它多常是答案都成立，不许写“通常”“拿不准就选”“永远别选”。因此“对不上就选它”要改成“某个列出的说法是你结论的削弱版才选它”。小试验（80道训练题各做2次，解题模型deepseek，约98万token，token是模型计费的文字单位）：这类规则使含该选项的题正确率从6.7%升到18.9%（11题变好、1题变差，显著），但与被禁止的“直接选它”效果相同；其余题略降、不显著；整体+4.4分、不显著。建议采用三条标准和已测过的审核提示词（40条真实规则无误伤），LiveMath成绩分开报告，并用“把这句当错误干扰项插入”的训练题检验（脚本已备好，约48万token，未运行）。

evidence:
MEASURED, pool: 283 training items (155 train part + 128 val part). The meta option is present in 129 (68+61) and is the reference in 129/129. Zero other "none of the above"-type options. Meta letter positions A23 B24 C28 D20 E34. Options are theorem statements (median first line 176 characters on meta items). 217/283 questions ask for the strongest/sharpest statement, in meta items (98/129) and non-meta items (119/154) alike.

MEASURED, v3 s3 cells (100 items x 2 runs, same items in both chains):
- E-ds: 75/200 pass; meta cells 5/90 (every pass is a meta pick); non-meta 70/110; D1 79 of 125 failures (63.2%).
- I-ds: 66/200 pass; meta 4/90; non-meta 62/110; D1 85 of 134 (63.4%).
- D1 occurs on no non-meta item.

MEASURED, D1 replies (164; GLM single-vote labels, my 30-reply manual check agrees 29/30):
- Meta option never mentioned 84 (51.2%); dismissed without an item-specific argument 61 (37.2%); rejected as "the chosen one is already the strongest" 15 (9.1%); acknowledged a stronger result may hold 4 (2.4%).
- Claims to recall the specific theorem 100 (61.0%); compares strength among listed options 119 (72.6%).
- Explicit "no option matches my result" in only 4/164 (a lower bound), and each time the solver picked the closest listed statement. Worked case 202604:10: the solver noticed option A's added restriction p < infinity and explained it away; it did the same under the structural rule.

MEASURED, v3 rule fates:
- I-ds s3-r1 quoted the sentence, so the mechanical option_text check dropped it (deterministic).
- E-ds s3-r1 (paraphrase) was refused by the adjudicator in v3. Re-asked under the identical prompt it was refused in only 1 of 5 votes.
- Over v3, the adjudicator made 41 calls on 38 rules and refused 2.

MEASURED, adjudicator probes:
- v3 prompt: split votes on 5/12 first-pass texts. It refuses the assignment's example N1 ("no match -> meta") 3/3, but keeps the anti-meta defaults N5/N6 by 2/3: asymmetric.
- First-pass addendum: the final intended verdict on 19/19 texts, all unanimous at 3/3.
- Refined addendum: over-refuses the generic heuristic N3 3/3, so it is not recommended.
- Collateral check of the recommended addendum: 39/40 texts unchanged; 1 new refusal (I-ds s3-r4, "the more likely correct statement"), which I judge correct.

MEASURED, pilot (deepseek-v4-flash, 80 training items = 45 meta + 35 non-meta, x 2 runs, 660/660 cells scored, 984,776 tokens):
- Meta items: parent 6/90, structural 17/90, blind 20/90, structural-first 17/90, blind-first 15/90.
- Structural vs parent on meta items: 11 up / 1 down / 33 tie, +0.122 [0.044, 0.200], p = 0.006.
- Structural vs blind: 8 up / 8 down, p = 1.0.
- Non-meta items: parent 42/70, structural 38/70 (40/70 if bare letters are accepted), p = 0.77.
- All 80 items: +0.044 [-0.031, 0.119], p = 0.15.
- 20/45 meta items get no meta pick in any of 10 cells. 8 of the blind rule's 20 meta picks are bare answers, against 1/17 for the structural rule. Structural gave 6/160 bare-letter format failures, parent 0/160.
- Real v3 21-item trigger panel: structural +1.5 items (4 up / 1 down, p = 0.375), borderline for C1.

ESTIMATED: on a LiveMath stage with 45% meta items, +2.4 points (if the non-meta loss is real) to +5.5 points (if it is noise). No transfer to similar benchmarks by construction.

CLAIM (unverified): the sealed test items share the 100%-reference property.
design:
BOUNDARY. A rule that names an option kind is an allowed task-structure rule iff all three hold:
(a) Public derivability: everything follows from the task card and the option's own wording; nothing from reference answers, scores, or training frequencies.
(b) Distribution invariance in both directions: the advice is equally right whether that option kind is the answer in 5% or 95% of its appearances. No frequency, prior, default, preference, tie-break, "usually", "more likely", "when in doubt" or "never", towards or away from the option.
(c) Content-conditional choice: the rule recommends the option only under the option's own condition, established by the solver on the item. For the meta option: a listed statement is true AND the solver names how the setup supports something stronger (an added hypothesis, a narrower range or class, a worse constant/exponent/bound, one direction of an equivalence, a dropped conclusion). Uncertainty, the mere presence/position/wording of the option, and a bare "my result matches no option" do not count.

"Same footing, not favoured" is allowed. Rules naming no option kind fall outside this clause.

The assignment's example ("if your computed answer matches no option, choose the meta option") is a fallback by this test. "Matches no option" is also true when the solver's own result is weaker than the theorem or wrong, so it pays off only because the meta option is always right on this pool. Its allowed form: "if the sharpest result you can establish is not listed but a listed statement is a true weakening of it, choose the meta option; if no listed statement is consistent with your result, re-check instead of defaulting". This form passes all prompts 3/3. Disclosure: I had pre-registered N1 as "allow"; the change is post hoc and argued, not voted.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- R1: put the policy as a registration clause and in the analyst instructions (exact text in report section 8).
- R2: append the tested first-pass addendum verbatim to ADJUDICATE_SYSTEM; keep reason-then-label plus a 3-vote majority. Do not add untested clarifications.
- R3: do not use any meta-option rule as the analyst's worked example.
- R4: report every LiveMath number split into meta / non-meta items, with the meta pick rate and the bare-answer share; a gain that falls >= 80% on meta items is labelled "option-format handling".
- R5: falsification panel. On the 55 non-meta s3 training items, put the meta sentence in as a false distractor and count meta picks per arm. This makes criterion (b) measurable; script prepared.
- R6 (owner decision): define the option in the LiveMath task card, so that learning is measured on top of a good instruction.
- R7 (optional): re-render the training pool. Corrected arithmetic: an always-pick-it solver nets 43 - 31f items per 100; R5 is preferred.

pilot.result:
Ran: 80 LiveMath TRAINING items (all 45 meta items of the v3 s3 draw + 35 seeded non-meta items) x 2 runs, deepseek-v4-flash (thinking off, temperature 0, max_tokens 32768), exact harness prompt layout and strict scorer; 660/660 cells scored, no truncation; arm texts verified constant across the 3 launch attempts.
- Meta items, cells passed: parent 6/90 (6.7%), structural rule 17/90 (18.9%), forbidden blind rule 20/90 (22.2%), structural-first 17/90, blind-first 15/90.
- Paired, structural vs parent on meta items: 11 up / 1 down / 33 tied, +12.2 points, 95% CI [+4.4, +20.0], sign p = 0.006 (still < 0.05 after x4 Bonferroni).
- Structural vs blind: 8 up / 8 down, p = 1.0 (indistinguishable).
- Non-meta items: 42/70 -> 38/70, 5 up / 7 down, p = 0.77; 2 of the 4 lost cells are bare-letter replies without the answer tag.
- All 80 items: +4.4 points [-3.1, +11.9], p = 0.15 (not significant).
- Real v3 21-item trigger panel: +1.5 items (borderline for C1).
- 20/45 meta items never moved under any arm; 8/20 of the blind rule's meta picks had no reasoning.
Verdict: a policy-conformant rule moves the solver on meta items, but on this pool its gain cannot be separated from the answer-distribution artifact.

risks:
1. Artifact (headline). On this pool a structural rule and an answer-distribution rule are rewarded identically (measured 8 up / 8 down between them). The gate cannot tell them apart; only the text policy, the R4 split and the R5 panel can. A LiveMath gain will be read as reasoning unless decomposed.
2. Small, local payoff. Estimated +2 to +5 points on the LiveMath stage, concentrated in a minority of items; the solver resists even an explicit instruction (22% of meta cells). No transfer to similar benchmarks by construction.
3. Statistics. The 45-item meta result is significant, but the 80-item net effect is not (p = 0.15). The real trigger-panel effect (+1.5 items) is borderline for C1; placebo controls and selftest were not simulated.
4. Adjudicator. GLM-5.3 at temperature 0 is non-deterministic (5/12 split under the v3 prompt). Most probe texts were written by me. The collateral check used 1 vote per concordant text and omitted colliding items/answer values. The N1 intended verdict changed after the probe (disclosed).
5. Format risk. The structural rule produced 6/160 bare-letter replies without the answer tag (parent 0/160).
6. A "name the weakening" rule could make the solver invent weakenings (D2 errors) on a pool where the option can be false; unmeasurable without R5.
7. The parent in the pilot was the LiveMath section only; its pass rates match the v3 chains on the same items.
8. Upstream construction and the test pool's 100% property are claims from training data only.
9. The first pass's pilot_analyse.py crashes on the final design; it is superseded by verify_pilot.py.
cost_estimate:
Spent by D7, measured: deepseek-v4-flash 984,776 tokens (pilot); GLM-5.3 about 411k (251,475 D1 labels, about 23k for the first-pass v3-prompt probe, 29,782 first-pass addendum probe, 54,455 no-match probe, 52,407 collateral check). Total about 1.40M.

Still to do, estimated:
- R1/R2/R4 (policy text, adjudicator addendum, reporting split): no API cost; an hour of editing plus the existing 3-vote majority.
- R5 one-time calibration (parent / structural / blind on 55 non-meta training items with the false distractor): about 0.48M deepseek tokens, about 1-3 hours on the token route at concurrency 6.
- R5 as a per-rule v5 check (rule arm only, parent shared): about 110 cells, about 0.16M tokens per rule naming an option kind. That is roughly 8% of a LiveMath gate round (about 2M tokens).
- R6 (task-card definition): no cost to write, but re-establishing the I-chain baseline needs a new LiveMath baseline run (100 items x 2 runs, about 0.3M tokens).
recommendation:
Adopt the boundary and enforce it in text now. It is cheap and tested, and it removes the v3 contradiction without opening an answer-distribution loophole.

1. Register the three-criterion option-kind clause (report section 8, R1), with "in both directions" and "a bare 'no match' is not the condition" spelled out for humans and the analyst.
2. Append the tested first-pass addendum verbatim to ADJUDICATE_SYSTEM (19/19 boundary texts as intended and unanimous; 0 false refusals on 38 real v3 rules + 2 generic sentences). Do not use my refined variant, which over-refused a generic heuristic.
3. Keep the mechanical quote drop, or let v4's template-option fix exempt the meta sentence (it occurs in 45.6% of items); the policy works either way.
4. Never give the analyst a meta-option rule as a worked example.
5. Make the meta / non-meta split mandatory for every LiveMath number, and label gains concentrated on meta items as "option-format handling", not generalizing experience learning.
6. Run the prepared falsification panel once (about 0.48M tokens) to calibrate parent / structural / blind. If it separates them, make it a v5 check for any rule that names an option kind.
7. Ask the owner whether the LiveMath task card should define the option. If the stage should measure learning beyond a good instruction, it should.

Expectations to communicate: a policy-conformant D1 rule is worth roughly +12 points on meta items and +2 to +5 on the stage, does not transfer, and cannot be shown to be reasoning rather than artifact on the current pool without step 6. Do not relabel the v3 LiveMath stage.
